crater-field.look: Relief reads straight away as a cratered moon: large flat floored craters with raised rims and central peaks, a power law of smaller craters, older ones erased inside young floors and fresh small ones on top. Slope sets the character from saturated highlands (2.0) to sparse scars in rough ground (3.0). The best graph attempt (FBm of clipped CellularDistance) gives only rimless overlapping dimples. At the top level alone, with occupancy 1, a lattice is obvious; with slope 2.2 to 2.4 the big craters thin out and the wide view looks irregular by eye, though the FFT keeps very faint straight streaks at the brick row orientation.

crater-field.range: measured -0.88 to 0.51 over 8 seeds at slope 2; -0.76 to 0.47 at slope 2.2; range shrinks with slope, port needs a normalising constant computed from the coarsest level's radius and occupancy
crater-field.artifacts: Single-level lattice at occupancy 1, and rows survive row shuffle. Composite has faint FFT streaks only. Dome/bowl 14.3/46.6 at h=0.01, against FBm Perlin 22.4/22.5.

crater-field.port_notes: Fold order is fixed: fine to coarse with erase, then additive replay levels. Erasing inside replay lifted pillars out of deep floors: c0ratio 3.1 and slope 57 before the fix, 7.7 and slope 5 after. Bowl, rim and ejecta all stay in the own cell, so no window is needed. Rays are only subtle star fringes and need an atan2 approximation, so leave them out of v1. Own-cell beat the colour fold, which was clean but less rich at scalar 797 ns for 4 levels.

A one-layer graph from existing nodes does give sparse, rimmed, flat-floored craters at 23.6/65/208 ns AVX2, so the graph baseline is better than reported, but it clips craters at Voronoi edges, has one scale and no erasure.

tournament.notes: Relief reads at once as a cratered moon: flat floors, raised rims, central peaks, small fresh craters on old floors. Re-test: c0 7.89 (7.6 at seed 3), range -0.76..0.47, far coords clean, 3D z-continuity max 0.0035. Scalar 708 ns 2D = 14.4x perlin2 at the stated set, not the reported 505.9. Flaws: the own-cell form caps crater size at one cell, so the top-level craters are one size class spaced one per cell, plainly visible at window 32; faint straight FFT streaks. A one-layer existing-node graph does give sparse rimmed flat-floored craters (23.6/65/208 ns AVX2) but clips them at Voronoi edges and has no multi-scale or erasure, so the node earns its place. Could be packaged with BubblePack as one own-cell multi-scale stamp node with a Shape enum. AVX2 cost unmeasured; prototyper estimate 16/18/22 ns looks optimistic.

master.one_liner: Multi-octave impact craters with destructive overprinting: floors erase older terrain and smaller craters, ejecta stacks additively, and late big impacts are replayed. Crater noise is known from planet generators; the erase-and-replay ordering is the variation.
master.look:
Prototype at 3 levels reads as a saturated cratered surface: bowls cut into older bowls, flat floors, rims broken by younger impacts. Spectrum shows no lattice dots at 16x window, axis stat high only because of the wide range, c0ratio 7.9. Also works as foam, cell-colony or hammered-metal texture with shallower depth.
[CraterField, nature-phenomena] Dense overlapping craters of many sizes, with old large craters degraded by small ones, like the lunar highlands. Hillshade from the own-cell, 9-octave prototype looks more convincing than the 3x3 window version.
master.algorithm:
Octave loop over radii with lacunarity about 1.6, existence probability giving N(D)~D^-2. At each octave, a crater's radius is at most 0.45 cell and centre jitter keeps it inside its own cell, so bowls in one octave never overlap and only the own-cell bowl need be tested. This removes any ordering seam.
Profile in r/R: floor flat or parabolic; raised rim; central peak if R>Rc; terraced inner wall bands for large R.
Compositing: m=smoothstep bowl mask; h=h*(1-m*Erase)+m*Depth*profile(r/R), then Ejecta added from the 3x3 window: rim blanket ~ (R/r)^3 with radial rays for young craters, angular variation from a small direction-to-noise polynomial hash.
Replay: after the fine octaves, rerun 1-2 coarse octaves with a different seed and low probability, so a few large young craters erase small ones (saturated terrain and fresh scars together).

[CraterField, stamp-scatter] Trick (colour fold): any non-commutative fold over stamps must apply them in one global order, or it seams where window contents change. Assign each lattice cell a colour from (ix mod 3, iy mod 3,...). Any 3-wide window holds exactly one cell of each colour, and that cell is computed directly, per lane, without search: g_axis(c) = 3*floor((floor(p_axis)+1-c_axis)/3) + c_axis. Loop colours c = 0..3^dim-1 (constant count) so the order is the same everywhere. For each level l of L, lattice scale s_l = Base*2^l, processed large to small: for each colour: f = feature of g, r = rad(h) <= 1 cell. t = |p-c|/r. Profile: bowl (t<0.75): 0.9*(t^2/0.5625-1)+0.35, rim fading to 0 at t=1. Flood weight fl = 1 - smoothstep(0.55,0.85,t). h = lerp(h, floorRef_i, fl) + r*Depth*profile*(1-smoothstep(0.9,1,t)). floorRef is the stamp's hash height, or the Source sampled at the crater centre (one eval per crater). Height units scale by 1/s_l so depth is proportional to diameter. Level density p_l = Density*2^(-b*(L-1-l)) gives crater size-frequency slope b. Optional Base Source is added as initial h.
master.why_new: CellularDistance F1 gives identical cone bowls with no rim, no size variation, no overlap logic. Every planet tool (Gaea Craterfield, KSP VoronoiCraters, Elite's geology inputs, World Creator) has a dedicated crater primitive; it is the first thing people try to fake with Worley and fail.
master.simd_plan:
Per-octave cost is one hash and one sqrt plus about 15 ops, so 9 octaves are estimated at 7-9 ns in any dimension (about 7x Perlin, 2x CellularDistance in 2D; under 1x in 3D; 0.2x in 4D). Use d*d rather than the prototype's pow. Base is a source evaluation only once.
[CraterField, stamp-scatter] Colour loop replaces offset loop; 1 hash and 1 profile per colour, with Selects. Per level 9/27/81 cells. Estimate 2D at L=3: 27 cell evals ~20 ns; 3D at L=2-3 (craters on planet surface from 3D position): 54-81 cells ~60-80 ns; 4D for tiling at L=2: 162 cells, ~180 ns. Justified as a specialist node. Uses Sqrt once per cell; no Pow per lane if the level table is computed at set time.
master.continuity: C0 verified: c0ratio 7.27-7.9. Each profile reaches zero weight by t=1, and t<1 is only possible within the window. Slope is bounded by Depth, so C1 fails only at the bowl-rim joint (could be smoothed).
master.params: Base Source (hybrid), Octaves (int), Lacunarity, Density Slope, Erase (0-1), Rim Height, Central Peak Radius, Ray Strength, Replay Octaves (int).
master.risks:
Not tested. Non-overlap constraint within an octave limits density and can give too-even spacing at the largest scale. Rays need a decent cheap angular function to avoid visible direction bands.
[CraterField, stamp-scatter] Colour 8 is always on top; I saw no 3-cell period in the FFT, but a very low density field might show it. Output is order-sensitive so GenPositionArray parity is fine, but an implementer must keep level and colour order constant across feature sets. Range needs a measured constant; proto clamps. Floor reference from Source at centres adds up to 3^dim evals per level, so make it optional.
[CraterField, nature-phenomena] Base terrain and profile amplitudes must be normalised over octaves; the range is not analytic if a source is attached. Lattice alignment of the coarsest octave may show at wide zoom. Size distribution is a hand-tuned power law, not a fitted Neukum function.
master.cost_note: Own-cell form: 9 octaves about 7-9 ns in any dimension (7x Perlin in 2D). With an ejecta window: 20-35 ns in 2D for 5 octaves plus 2 replays.
master.variant_notes: Five proposals of order-dependent crater overprint. Two ways of making order global: per-octave own-cell craters with no overlap inside an octave (cheapest, about 7-9 ns), or the colour-ordered window fold, which works for any non-commutative stamp. 3D on planet positions avoids polar distortion.

bubble-pack.look: True round discs over about a 10:1 size range, separated, with small ones in the gaps between large ones. Threshold panel shows clean non-overlapping circles. 3D: solid mode gives clearly round isolated vesicles (cheese or pumice), ball mode gives a pile of real spheres. Per-bubble value mode reads as coins or pebbles. The nearest graph I could build (Max of 4 scaled sqrt CellularDistance layers) overlaps and merges blobs and gives a connected sponge instead. Default settings at rmax 0.48 showed a blatant square lattice; with rmax 0.38, occupancy ramp 0.5 to 1 and lacunarity 1.4 it is gone from the close view, and only very faint horizontal rows remain in the 4x wide view if you look for them.

bubble-pack.artifacts: The top-level lattice is real: rmax=0.48 gives axis 182 with visible rows and columns. Tuned set: axis 28.4, isoCV 0.78, clean FFT, faint rows only in the 4x wide view. Half the area is flat, so terrain use needs a base.

Clipping children to the ancestor cell removes all overlap but cut coverage from 47% to 24% (measured on the near-identical set with rmax=0.36, on=0.6), so I rejected it. Row shuffle helped less than lowering rmax and top occupancy, so it is not needed. Rotations are per-level constants.

master.one_liner: Non-overlapping multi-scale sphere packing evaluated pointwise, with no window at all, for foam, droplets, pumice vesicles and pebble mosaics.
master.look: Clean domes at several scales: large bubbles with progressively smaller ones filling the gaps, with almost no overlap. The field reads as bubble raft, foam or droplets. A 3D threshold should give pumice or basalt vesicles and Swiss-cheese caves, though only the 2D form was prototyped.
master.algorithm: For level k in a fixed loop: P=Rot_k*x*f_k; C=floor(P); h=hash(C); r=rmin+(rmax-rmin)*r3 (rmax<=0.48); m=C+r+(1-2r)*(r1,r2), which keeps the disc inside its own cell. World centre cw=Rot_k^-1*(m/f_k); rw=r/f_k. For each ancestor a<k: Q=Rot_a*cw*f_a; ha=hash(floor(Q)); recover that cell's disc (ma,ra,on) with the same formula; if on, rw=min(rw,(|Q-ma|-ra)/f_a). Then rw=max(rw,0); d=|P-m|/f_k; cap=sqrt(max(rw^2-d^2,0)); H=max(H,cap*on_k). Because each disc is confined to its cell, only the sample's own cell can contain it, so no 3^D search is needed. Clearance is tested at the child's centre, so each bubble stays a true circle or sphere.
master.why_new: Random non-overlapping packing normally needs dart throwing or a global pass, which FastNoise forbids. Size-jittered cellular cells overlap or collide, and Simplex blobs are not round. A graph of existing nodes cannot give the clearance test.
master.simd_plan: Loops are fixed and ancestor lookups are lane-wise since cw differs per lane. L levels need L(L+1)/2 hashes, independent of dimension: 15 hashes for 5 levels, estimated at 8-10 ns in any dimension (about 8x Perlin in 2D, 2.5x CellularDistance in 2D, under 1x in 3D, 0.25x in 4D). Use fixed per-level rotation matrices; output is analytic in [0, rmax/f0].
master.continuity: C0: cap reaches 0 at the rim, with infinite slope there because of the sqrt (an output mode using 1-d^2/rw^2 avoids that). Dense scanlines: 0 jumps. Own-cell and full 3x3 evaluation differ by mean 4e-7, max 0.006.
master.params: Levels (int), Level Scale, Radius Min/Max, Fill (hybrid), Output {Dome, Wall, Bubble Value}.
master.risks: Confinement to rotated square cells can leave a faint lattice in the largest level. Output is zero outside bubbles, so gaps stay flat unless more levels are added. A child can slightly overlap an ancestor from a neighbouring cell. Ancestor lookup makes high level counts grow quadratically.
master.cost_note: L levels need L(L+1)/2 hashes, independent of dimension: 15 hashes for 5 levels, estimated at 8-10 ns in any dimension (about 8x Perlin in 2D, 2.5x CellularDistance in 2D, under 1x in 3D, 0.25x in 4D).

cumulus-noise.look: 3D iso: round boulders whose surfaces are covered by smooth nested sub-domes with clean veined creases. Level 1 is big soft lobes, level 2 reads as cauliflower or brain coral, level 3 gets intricate. This is the only one of the family with true florets nested on a parent surface, and it looks unlike FBm, billow, puffy caps and the graph caps at the same view. Flaws seen: parents are over-even (one lattice, similar size) unless the radius is modulated, the mod view gives towers and gaps but is still packed spheres rather than a cloud silhouette, and the raw 2D height has radial creases inside each parent because displacement depends only on direction. So the 2D use is threshold or cut at iso, where it gives scalloped discs.
cumulus-noise.dims: 2D and 3D rendered. 4D not written; true 4D lattices are estimated at about 120 ns and a w-phase form was not tested.
cumulus-noise.range: measured -0.80 to 0.66 over 8 seeds with gain 1.2; clamped to [-1,1]; iso 0 is the surface
cumulus-noise.artifacts: FFT shows a star of streaks, axis about 24, which I attribute to straight parent edges and radial creases in the 2D field. Parents are over-even in the wide view. Dome/bowl 27.9/11.6 at h=0.01 with saddle 60.5%: the 2D field is pleated, so this metric does not describe the 3D surface.
cumulus-noise.node_shape: Levels (1-3), Lacunarity, Height, Radius Min/Max (hybrid), Child Radius Min/Max, Parent Blend, Child Edge, Rim Softness, Output {Signed, Density}
cumulus-noise.port_notes: The two-parent blend as specified still jumped (c0ratio about 1.0 to 1.2). The fixes tried were: own children by power distance and parents by signed distance d-R (levels=0 went from 1.14 to 8.00), fade displacement at parent and child centres (levels=2 went from 1.41 to 3.78), and fade the next level at owner boundaries. One child chain, with displacement fading to zero at the parent boundary, then looked as good at about 60% of the two-parent scalar 3D cost (639.1 vs 1053.8 ns). Final c0ratio 4.91, max slope 14. I attribute the remainder to child cap rims, but did not isolate it.

tournament.notes: 3D vol: round boulders covered by nested sub-domes with veined creases, the only true lobes-on-a-parent-surface result in the family and unlike FBm, billow or the cap graphs; the Add(Cap 90, 0.25 x Cap 30) graph gives bumpy boulders without nesting or creases, about 60 percent of the look. Re-test: c0 4.91, max slope 14, range -0.80..0.66, far coords clean, 3D z-continuity max 0.0075, scalar 256.6 ns 2D = 5.05x perlin2, as reported. Flaws: the 2D field is radial pleats in Voronoi-like cells, not clouds, so 2D use is threshold only; parents over-even (dense even lattice at seed 5 window 12, axis 40.9 not 24) and packed spheres even with modulation; FFT star. Port is two 3x3x3 power-distance searches plus projection and several fades, estimated 40 ns 3D and 120 ns 4D: an example scene, not a building block.

master.one_liner: Bumps-on-bumps via surface projection: the nearest Cellular sphere is radially displaced by a finer Cellular dome field evaluated at the point's projection onto that sphere, recursively, giving true cauliflower florets and cumulus billows instead of FBm cusps.
master.look: 3D iso: spheres covered with round sub-domes which are themselves covered with smaller domes: cauliflower, romanesco, cumulus congestus towers, brain coral, moss cushions. Unlike Perlin-Worley clouds (cusped, noisy) the florets are properly nested and round, with clean creases between them. 2D slice: lumpy discs with scalloped outlines, directly usable as cloud sprites or lichen patches.
master.algorithm:
Level 0: Cellular F1 search (3x3x3) at scale 1 returning nearest centre c0, its radius R0 (size jitter) and second-nearest (c0b, R0b, F2).
 n = normalize(p - c0); q = c0 + R0 * n                  // projection onto the parent sphere
 Level 1: Cellular F1 at scale s (Lacunarity, e.g. 3) evaluated at q (not p): nearest centre c1, radius R1; dome1 = Max(0, 1 - |q - c1|^2 / R1^2)   // round dome on the parent surface
 Level 2 (optional): n1 = normalize(q - c1); q2 = c1 + R1*n1; dome2 = dome at scale s^2 evaluated at q2
 Reff = R0 + Height*(dome1 + dome2/s)                     // displaced radius
 sdfA = |p - c0| - Reff
 Repeat the child evaluation for the second-nearest parent (c0b) -> sdfB; blend weight wb = SmoothStep(0, Blend, F2 - F1); sdf = Lerp(Min(sdfA, sdfB), sdfA, wb) (two parents keep the switch of nearest parent continuous).
Output: Signed sdf (scaled) or Density = Clamp(-sdf/Height) for volumetric clouds. 2D: circles with bumps (projection onto the circle, 2D cellular at q). 4D: w as phase for the cellular jitter (3D lattice) or true 4D lattices per level.
master.why_new: FBm-of-inverted-Worley displaces throughout the volume, so bumps do not sit on the parent surface and successive octaves do not nest; the projection trick anchors each level to the surface below it, which no graph can do (needs the parent's centre and radius inside the child evaluation).
master.simd_plan: Three Cellular-style window searches (nearest centre + radius + distance) in sequence, with the two-parent blend doubling levels 1-2: 3D roughly 3-5x CellularDistance 3D (40-60 ns), 2D ~4x Cellular 2D (15 ns). All Select-based; normalize via InvSqrt. 4D: 3D lattice with w-phase jitter at the same cost; true 4D lattices would be ~5x Cellular 4D and are not recommended.
master.continuity: C0: the dome displacement and sphere union are continuous; the nearest-parent switch is smoothed by the F2-F1 blend (without it the field has small jumps in the gaps between parent spheres, the iso-surface at 0 usually not).
master.params: Levels (int 1-2), Lacunarity, Height (bump height fraction of R0), SizeJitter per level, Blend width, Output enum (Signed/Density), Feature Scale, Seed.
master.risks: Expensive; the two-parent blend only hides the switch near the Voronoi boundary of the two nearest parents, three-way corners can still show a kink. Child domes inherit the parent's spherical parametrisation so they stretch slightly near the parent's equator relative to lattice spacing.
master.cost_note: Three Cellular-style window searches (nearest centre + radius + distance) in sequence, with the two-parent blend doubling levels 1-2: 3D roughly 3-5x CellularDistance 3D (40-60 ns), 2D ~4x Cellular 2D (15 ns).

puffy-caps.look: Height view: broccoli or cumulus tops, every lobe round at every scale, thin dark creases. 3D iso at 0.47: separated cauliflower clumps with bumps on bumps, really different from FBm Perlin. But a graph of existing nodes (FractalFBm of SignedSquareRoot(Max(CellularDistance EuclideanSquared with Size Jitter, 0))) rendered through fnlab gives the same look in 2D, relief and 3D iso. Only small differences: the graph's lobes are a bit more even in size.

puffy-caps.range: measured -0.97 to 0.92 over 8 seeds (analytic bound [-1,1]); mean +0.27, so it is skewed high
puffy-caps.artifacts: No lattice seen in the FFT or wide view. The weakness is redundancy, not artifacts. Dome/bowl 48.4/13.3 at h=0.01, against the graph form's 46.3/13.4 (scalar reference, single radius) and FBm Perlin's 22.4/22.5.
puffy-caps.node_shape: If kept at all: Octaves, Gain, Lacunarity, Radius Min, Radius Max, Softness. Better shipped as a graph preset.
puffy-caps.port_notes: c0ratio 3.34 is consistent with the infinite sqrt slope at the rim; the softened profile sqrt(best+s^2)-s at s=0.1 measures 6.37. The 3x3 window is exact for R<=1 because points stay in their own cell. If NestedCaps becomes a node, this is its no-nesting mode.

master.one_liner: A fractal sum of spherical-cap layers that gives cauliflower and cumulus tops: convex lobes on lobes, where FBm and billow give creases and blobs.
master.look: Hillshade looks like broccoli, cumulus tops or botryoidal mineral: every lobe is convex at every scale. The contact sheet has nothing like it.
master.algorithm: H=0; a=1; f=f0. For octave o: X=Rot_o*x*f+offset_o; best=0; for each jittered cell in the 3^D window: r2=|X-p_i|^2; best=max(best,R_i^2-r2) with R_i=0.55+0.45*r3. H+=a*sqrt(best)/f; a*=gain; f*=lacunarity. Taking max of (R^2-r^2) and a single sqrt per octave is exactly the max of caps, with no per-cell sqrt.
master.why_new: Abs(noise) billow gives long sinuous creases and irregular domes; a sum of circular caps has convex, round lobes. A graph could approximate it only by a separate CellularDistance chain per octave, with Sqrt and Add nodes, and it would pay extra per-cell InvSqrt and F-slot work.
master.simd_plan: No per-cell sqrt or distance sort. Estimated 3 ns per octave in 2D, so 5 octaves are about 15 ns (3x FBm of Perlin); 48 ns in 3D (4x FBm); 160 ns in 4D. Own-cell and 2^D shortcuts failed: 2^D corners showed lattice blocks, jittered corners showed fine cross-hatch, and own-cell showed a grid of balls at the coarse octave. A mix may work (3x3 for coarse octaves, own-cell or corners for fine ones), but my one mix test still showed cross-hatch.
master.continuity: C0: caps meet at creases where the max switches, and the outer edge has infinite slope only where the coverage gaps reach 0. Jittered windows with R up to 1.0 cover the plane well, though a cap can reach beyond the 3x3 window at high jitter (not measured).
master.params: Octaves (int), Gain, Lacunarity, Radius Min/Max, Radius Jitter (hybrid).
master.risks: Cost is several times FBm in 3D and 4D, and the cheap paths were rejected visually. Output range needs a measured constant. A related SDF form (clipped smooth union of spheres, so bumps exist only near a base surface) gave cloud-like silhouettes but looked less striking as a height field; it may suit 3D iso-surfaces and was not rendered in 3D. The fBm-of-SDF idea is from my memory of Quilez's writing, as the article URL returned 404.
master.cost_note: Estimated 3 ns per octave in 2D, so 5 octaves are about 15 ns (3x FBm of Perlin); 48 ns in 3D (4x FBm); 160 ns in 4D.

sphere-fractal.look: Carve mode: strong pumice, round pits inside round pits with sharp rims. But a 7 node graph (MinSmooth chain of CellularDistance on Perlin) rendered through fnlab gives the same look, only denser. Union mode: never reached cumulus in about 18 renders. It reads as gravel, cobbles or a raspberry: a crust of round grains with real overhangs in a thin shell on the base, which FBm and simple graphs do not give. The base stays smooth underneath. The 2D slice and height view are dull: a smooth base with slightly bubbly patches.
sphere-fractal.dims: 3D rendered. 2D output is a z slice of the 3D function; a true 4 corner 2D form and 4D were not written.
sphere-fractal.range: clamped to [-1,1]; measured -1 to 1 over 8 seeds in union mode. Output is distance-like, not normalised, gain needs choosing by the user.
sphere-fractal.artifacts: Rows were obvious at jitter 0.2 with an axis-aligned first octave, and not visible after rotation plus jitter 0.3. One 5 octave sphere-base render had faint diagonal grain. Dome/bowl on the height slice is 25.2/25.0, near FBm, so the 2D form adds nothing.
sphere-fractal.node_shape: Base Source, Mode {Union, Carve}, Octaves, Scale, Lacunarity, Clip, Blend Clip, Blend Surface, Radius Min, Radius Max, Jitter
sphere-fractal.port_notes: The corner lattice's value outside the balls is not exact across cells by construction. With r + margin + jitter <= 1, every ball closer than the margin is among the 2^D corners, so min(q, margin) is exact and C0: measured c0ratio 8.00. 8 corners looked as good as a 27 cell window on a plane. Rotate from octave 0 and use jitter of about 0.3. Unsolved flaw: clip, base gradient and sphere scale are coupled, and a wrong base fills the box.

tournament.notes: Carve mode is good pumice but the prototyper's own 7-node fnlab graph (3 octaves plus Perlin, 14.7/42.9/133 ns AVX2) gives the same look in the comparison image. Union mode at seed 5 is a thin gravel crust on a smooth Perlin surface, grit rather than cobbles, and never cumulus. The 2D sheet is a smooth base with bubbly patches. Re-test: scalar 256 ns 2D = 5.0x perlin2; c0 8.0 and clean far coords reproduced in the first pass. The corner-lattice margin clamp (exact and C0 when r + margin + jitter <= 1) is worth a note for any sphere-distance field. Usability flaw is real: clip, base gradient and sphere scale are coupled.

master.one_liner: Fractal of real spheres in distance space: carve mode gives multi-scale pumice and swiss-cheese voids, union mode grows cauliflower cumulus or rubble on any base field.
master.look: Prototyped. Carve: golf-ball and pumice crust with craters at several scales, strong at 3 octaves. Union: crumbly cauliflower or rubble clumps around a Perlin base; with these parameters it looks gravelly, and needs larger S0, 2 to 3 octaves and bigger smin to read as cumulus. 2D slice: discs on discs (bubbly edge) or Apollonian-like holes. For clouds, rocks, moss, sponges, bread, coral.
master.algorithm: Base d (source treated as SDF units, or constant for carve). s=S0. Loop Octaves: q = grid(R_o p / s)*s, where grid is min over the 2^dim corners of floor(p): corner sphere radius r = Rmin + (Rmax-Rmin)*rnd01(hash), distance |f - corner| - r. Union mode (cumulus): q = smax(q, d - Clip*s, Ka*s); d = smin(q, d, Kb*s). Clipping makes detail appear only in a shell around the current surface, so puffs stack on puffs (after iq's SDF fBm). Carve mode (pumice): d = smax(d, -q, Kb*s). Per octave use fixed rotation R (table) and lacunarity ~2. Each sphere must satisfy r + jitter <= corner reach. Optional RadiusBias: r scales with exp(-d/s) so puffs shrink away from surface. Sphere-sized distribution from rnd01 sets pore-size power law.
master.why_new: FBm adds values, so it can never make round overhanging lobes; here lobes are real spheres and output keeps a distance-like bounded gradient, so sphere tracing and meshing behave. A graph equivalent needs 3 nodes per octave with parameters scaled by hand and shares no rotation. Not visually near anything on the sheet, particularly in 3D.
master.simd_plan: Constant octave loop; 2^dim hash+sqrt per octave, plus smin/smax. 3D: about 2.5 ns per octave, so 4 octaves about 10 ns plus source. 2D 1 ns per octave; 4D 16 corners, about 5 ns per octave. Hash per corner uses the current octave's seed.
master.continuity: C0 at least; C1 mostly due to smin and smax, except at grid transitions where radii must fit reach. Grid reach limited so no seams when r <= reach.
master.params: Source (base), Mode enum, Octaves (int), S0 (float), Lacunarity, Clip (hybrid), Ka, Kb, Rmin, Rmax, RadiusBias.
master.risks: Parameter sensitivity: clip plus dense spheres dilates surface, and earlier test filled the whole box until tuned (base amplitude and clip must relate). Base must be roughly unit-gradient, so pair with LevelSetDistance or bound its range. The union mode is near iq's known technique; hierarchy and carve with distribution are the variation. Fine-scale octaves alias.
master.cost_note: 3D: about 2.5 ns per octave, so 4 octaves about 10 ns plus source. 2D 1 ns per octave; 4D 16 corners, about 5 ns per octave.
